answer: An agent market requires every identity, whether named willow, cedar, or opal, to lock a bond of 100 tokens before bidding, and caps its concurrent jobs at five. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore requires locking 100,000 tokens; splitting the same funds among more names buys no extra job capacity. The defense makes influence scale with committed capital, so an attacker pays the opportunity cost of immobilizing funds for every active identity.
